resources.string: NFC is on. Open Scan to read a tag or Write to program one.
Enable NFC in system settings; the app cannot read or write tags while it is off.
This device has no NFC chip. Scanning and writing stay unavailable; other screens remain for reference.
Read and decode a nearby tag.
Compose a message and write it to a tag.
History view lands in milestone M4; task profiles in M5. This screen shows only real device state, never sample tag data.
Allowlisted actions, confirmation policy and a local execution log are milestone M5 work. Tag payloads are never auto-executed.
Local scan history, search, favourites and export are milestone M4 work. No scan data is stored yet.
Theme, privacy and export preferences follow the persistence milestone (M4). The app currently follows the system theme.
Reader mode is active on this screen. Unlock the phone, hold the tag flat against the antenna (usually the back of the phone) and keep it still.
Hold another tag to replace this result.
Identifiers can be absent, randomised on every scan, or shared between tags. Do not use them for identity or access control.
Live read failed; showing the content Android cached when the tag was discovered.
This tag is not NDEF-formatted (or Android exposes no Ndef technology for it).
The tag exposes NdefFormatable; it can be formatted from the Write screen after confirmation.
The tag holds data that is not valid NDEF. It is shown as unreadable rather than guessed.
The content could not be read. Hold the tag still and scan again.
Preview truncated to the first 4096 bytes.
Values are reported by Android without extra radio traffic. A technology name does not mean protected data can be accessed.
This link uses a scheme or characters NFC Studio does not open (only http, https, mailto, tel, sms and geo). You can still copy it.
Warning: the link contains text before “@”. The real destination is the host shown above.
Warning: the host contains non-Latin characters that can imitate another site.
Note: plain http is not encrypted.
No app could open this link.
The tag was moved or removed too soon. Hold it steady until the operation finishes.
The tag session expired. Lift the tag and hold it again.
This tag does not support NDEF.
The message needs %1$d B but this tag holds at most %2$d B.
The read-back did not match what was sent. The tag content may be incomplete; scan it to check.
Android rejected the message as invalid NDEF.
This tag or phone cannot make the tag read-only.
The tag refused to become read-only. Its content is unchanged.

plurals.item: Ready to write %1$d record (%2$d bytes). Keep the tag still until it finishes.
Ready to write %1$d records (%2$d bytes). Keep the tag still until it finishes.

resources.string: Hold the tag against the antenna. You will be asked to confirm before anything changes.
Do not move the tag until this finishes.
Read back and verified: content matches (%1$d B).
The write completed, but the tag could not be read back in the same session (it was removed, or it was just formatted). Scan it to check.
This tag holds %1$s. Writing replaces it and the previous content cannot be recovered from this app.
This tag is not NDEF-formatted. Formatting changes how the tag stores data, may not be reversible, and cannot be undone from this app.
data that is not valid NDEF
content that could not be read
Text is longer than 8 KiB, which no common tag can hold.
Use a language code such as en, de or pt-BR.
Enter a valid http(s), mailto, tel, sms or geo URI without spaces.
Use a lowercase MIME type such as text/plain or application/json.
Both ask for confirmation after a tag is detected and show what it currently holds.
This tag holds %1$s. Clearing writes an empty NDEF record. It does not securely erase every memory location on the chip.
Making a tag read-only is irreversible on most tags: no app, including this one, can change its content afterwards. After you continue, hold the tag; you will be asked once more.
This tag holds %1$s. After locking, it can never be rewritten or cleared.
The tag reported success and is now read-only.
